entry.hops: No wire in the Node test: the daemon client is the real session service called in process (handleCall).
entry.notRun: no real runtime or store; the daemon client is the service called in-process
entry.runs: apps/desktop/src/main/session-host.ts SessionHost (setVisibleSessions, submitToSession, prefetchSession, subscribeSessionStates) over the real createSessionService (idle eviction sweep, handleCall session.*) with a scripted stored session and runtime, node:test mock timers, the read-diagnostics sink

normalised.reason: per-run temp path (or generated name) replaced by a placeholder

product.tree: product tree loaded by the recorder

replay.compare: mixdog-core-session + mixdog-app-server (session host re-entry): replay each step list on a virtual clock (mock timers: Date, setInterval, setTimeout from 1_800_000_000_000; tick values are in the step labels); compare published texts, service size, stored read count and diagnostics records after each step
replay.entry: Six cases: a built mixdogd over its real WebSocket listener, the desktop protocol client (packages/protocol-client connect, sessionReducer, sessionStateOf) as the desktop, a second client as the old runtime that writes while the desktop is away; the desktop's outgoing reads are counted and can be held on the socket (a read in flight). The replayed submission id: thread/start then turn/start twice with one clientSubmissionId into the session actor (actor.rs Submissions::join).

declared.steps[].serviceSize: how many runtimes Node's session service holds: the desktop host's bookkeeping, shown to no user
declared.steps[].storedReads: Node's host store-read counter; the reads the desktop sends are compared instead where a case is about them (readsUnchanged, readsSinceOpen)
declared.steps[].updateCount: how many updates Node's host published to its listener
declared.steps[].lastUpdate.frameSource: whether Node's host built the frame from the live runtime or a stored replay. The desktop forwards it (desktop-service-client.ts:564) and acts on it: a replay frame never raises a turn notification (connections/server-notifier.ts:171, desktop-turn-notifier.ts:217). K1's client has no such field (packages/protocol-client carries none; the core's frames neither): a turn notification there comes from the live turn/completed event of the core, which a resume or read snapshot never carries, so a stored read cannot notify; the rows the user sees are compared as texts
declared.steps[].lastUpdate.readTraceId, lastUpda: the read-tracing sink's correlation id: the desktop forwards it (desktop-service-client.ts:563) only to reportTranscriptRead (shared/transcript-read-diagnostics.ts), a diagnostics sink that draws nothing; the protocol client carries no such field
declared.performanceNowWhileHeld, performanceNowA: the recorder's scripted performance clock for the tracing sink
declared.outcome.rejected.message: the recorder's injected store failure text; the core's own read failure (a session the store does not hold) is the input, and the caller must get exactly the core's error (sameErrorObject)

normalised.texts: the desktop's user and assistant rows in order; the core writes a row only through a turn, so each row the recorder wrote into the store or the old runtime without a turn ('old progress N', 'persisted after leaving', 'cold refresh', 'stored answer', 'private saved answer') is the answer of a turn whose carrier prompt ('progress N', 'leave', 'cold', 'stored', 'saved') is left out of texts, as are the core's turn-end divider rows (kind turndone)
normalised.lastUpdate.snapshot.items[].id: the core mints its own item ids; rows are compared by text in order
normalised.clock: mock timers, not the shared fixed Date.now; performance.now reads the same mock clock (ms since the fixture started), except where a case scripts it (read tracing: 0, then 321)
normalised.dataDir: temp user-data dir not in the recording

replay.targetsCheckedAgainst: o1 6bf0a5bbf: each rust target exists at path:line, is declared `pub` and is reachable through `pub mod` or `pub use` from its crate root
